This chart-race video tracks the smartphone market’s biggest pivot: Apple’s iPhone momentum vs Android’s expanding volume—then the moment “share” stopped being the whole story because iPhone proved it could monetize with services even when unit share softened.

instagram_caption:
🚀 The iPhone Exodus vs Android Lock‑In: the smartphone race that changed everything.

For years, the story sounded simple: Apple sells premium iPhones, Android wins everywhere else. But the numbers tell a sharper tale—one where Android keeps stacking units while iPhone goes through cycles of lift, pause, and resilience. This is the dramatic timeline comparison of global smartphone shipments, visualized like a chart-race.

📱 2016–2018: Android’s volume engine keeps pulling ahead. In 2016, Android (non‑iPhone) shipments are about 1,224M units, rising to ~1,520M by 2018. Meanwhile iPhone shipments hover around ~216M in 2016–2018—strong, but not accelerating. Total market shipments grow from ~1,440M to ~1,736M.

⚡ 2019–2020: the “plateau vs shock” moment. In 2019, iPhone shipments drop from ~216M to ~191M, while Android still surges to ~1,595M. Then 2020 hits: overall demand compresses into a tough, uncertain year, but iPhone rebounds to ~206M and Android remains enormous at ~1,620M.

🔥 2021–2023: iPhone fights back; Android stays dominant. iPhone climbs to ~234M in 2021 and holds near ~235M in 2022. Android stays the volume titan—peaking around ~1,915M in 2021, then easing to ~1,585M by 2023 as the market cools. Total shipments fall from ~2,149M (2021) to ~1,811M (2023).

📈 2024–2026 (estimate): the next phase—Android re-accelerates while iPhone stabilizes. iPhone holds around ~230–231M in 2024–2025 and rises to ~235M in 2026. Android climbs from ~1,620M (2024) to ~1,700M (2025) and ~1,800M by 2026.

Here’s the twist: even when iPhone shipments don’t explode, Apple’s services “gravity” keeps the long-term game moving—so shipments show the battlefield, not the whole war.
